passages.source_text: Τρίτῃ δὲ ἡμέρᾳ εἰς τὸ προωρισμένον τῆς Τύρου χωρίον σὺν τοῖς οἰκειοτάτοις ἐλθὼν ἔγωγε εὑρίσκω τὸν Ἀππίωνα, Ἀννουβίωνός τε καὶ Ἀθηνοδώρου καθεζόμενον μέσον καὶ μετὰ πολλῶν ἄλλων τῶν ἐκ παιδείας ἀνδρῶν ἡμᾶς ἀναμένοντα. καὶ ὅμως οὐδὲν καταπλαγεὶς προσαγορεύσας ἀντικαθέζομαι τῷ Ἀππίωνι, ὃς μετ᾽ οὐ πολὺ λέγειν ἤρξατο Βούλομαι πρῶτος ἀρξάμενός ἐντεῦθεν ἤδη ταχέως ἐλθεῖν ἐπὶ τὸ ζητούμενον. πρὸ τοῦ σε, τέκνον Κλήμης, ἡμῖν παρεῖναι, Ἀνουβίων οὗτος καὶ Ἀθηνόδωρος, οἱ χθὲς ἅμα τοῖς ἄλλοις ἐπακούσαντές σου διαλεγομένου, ἀφηγήσαντό μοι πῶς ἐν τῇ Ῥώμῃ συνερχόμενός σοι ὡς ἐρῶντι πολλὰ τῶν θεῶν κατεψευσάμην, εἰπὼν αὐτοὺς παιδεράστας, ἀσελγεῖς, μιγνυμένους μητράσιν ἀδελφαῖς θυγατράσιν, καὶ μυρίαις μοιχείαις ἐνεχομένους. ἀλλ’ ἐχρῆν σε, ὦ τέκνον, εἰδέναι ὅτι μὴ τοιαῦτα περὶ θεῶν φρονῶν ἔγραφον, ἀλλὰ στοργῇ τῇ πρὸς σὲ τὰ ἀληθῆ λέγειν ἀπεκρυπτόμην, ἅπερ εἰ νῦν ἐθέλεις, παρ’ ἐμοῦ ἄκουσον.

τῶν πάλαι ἀνδρῶν οἱ σοφώτατοι, πᾶσαν ἀλήθειαν αὐτοὶ καμάτῳ μεμαθηκότες, τοὺς ἀναξίους καὶ μὴ ὀρεγομένους θείων μαθημάτων ἀπεκρύψαντο τὴν ἐπιστήμην λαβεῖν. οὔτε γὰρ ἀπ’ Οὐρανοῦ καὶ τῆς μητρὸς αὐτοῦ Γῆς γεγόνασιν παῖδες δώδεκα (ὡς ὁ μῦθος καταριθμεῖ, ἄρρενες μὲν Ὠκεανός, Κοῖος, Κρῖος, Ὑπερίων, Ἰαπετός, Κρόνος· θήλειαι δὲ Θεία, Θέμις, Μνημοσύνη, Δημήτηρ, Τηθύς, Ῥέα) οὔτε τῇ ἐξ ἀδάμαντος ἅρπῃ τὰ αἰδοῖα Κρόνος Οὐρανοῦ τοῦ πατρὸς ἐκτεμὼν (ὡς φατέ) εἰς βυθὸν ἀπέρριψεν. ἀλλ’ οὐδ’ ἐκ τῆς ἀποτομῆς τοῦ Οὐρανοῦ σταγόνων ῥυέντος αἵματος ἡ Ἀφροδίτη ἐγένετο οὐδ’ αὖ Κρόνος τῇ Ῥέᾳ μιγεὶς καὶ γεννήσας Πλούτωνα πρῶτον κατέπιεν, διὰ τινὰ Προμηθέως θεσμὸν δεδιὼς μήποτε γεννηθὲν ἐξ αὐτοῦ βρέφος, γενναιότερον αὐτοῦ γενόμενον ἀφέληται αὐτὸν τῆς βασιλείας. οὐ τὸν Ποσειδῶνα δεύτερον γεννήσας ὁμοίως κατέπιεν. οὐ μετὰ τούτους τὸν Δία γεννηθέντα ἡ μήτηρ κατακρύψασα ἡ Ῥέα ἀπαιτήσαντι τῷ Κρόνῳ καταπιεῖν λίθον ἀντέδωκεν, ὃς οὐ καταποθεὶς τοὺς προκαταποθέντας θλίψας ἐξῶσεν, ὡς προελθεῖν πρῶτον μὲν τὸν πρῶτον καταποθέντα Πλούτωνα, ἐπ’ αὐτῷ δὲ Ποσειδῶνα καὶ τρίτον τὸν Δία. οὐδέ γε (ὡς φασίν) μητρὸς προνοίᾳ διασωθεὶς ὁ Ζεὺς καὶ εἰς οὐρανὸν ἀναβάς, τὸν πατέρα τῆς βασιλείας καθεῖλεν. οὐ πατρὸς ἀδελφοὺς ἐκόλασεν. οὐκ εἰς πόθον γυναικῶν θνητῶν κατῆλθεν. οὐκ ἀδελφαῖς ἢ θυγατράσιν, οὐκ ἀδελφῶν γυναιξίν, οὐ παισὶν αἰσχρῶς συνεγένετο. οὐδὲ Μῆτιν γεννήσας κατέπιεν ...., ἵνα ἀπ’ ἐγκεφάλου μὲν τὴν Ἀθηνᾶν ἀναφύσῃ ἐκ τῆς Μήτιδος, ἐκ δὲ τοῦ μηροῦ τὸν Διόνυσον τέκῃ, ὃν ὑπὸ Τιτάνων ἐσπαράχθαι λέγουσιν. οὐ δεῖπνον ἐπὶ τῷ Θέτιδος καὶ Πηλέως γάμῳ συντελεῖ. οὐ τὴν Ἔριν τῶν γάμων ἀπεώσατο. οὐχ αὕτη ἡ Ἔρις ἀτιμασθεῖσα μάχην καὶ στάσιν τοῖς ἑστιωμένοις ἐπενόησεν. οὐ μῆλον χρύσεον ἐκ τῶν Ἑσπερίδων κήπων λαβοῦσα ἐπέγραψεν „δῶρον τῇ καλῇ“. ἔπειτα μυθολογοῦσιν ὡς Ἥρα τε καὶ Ἀθηνᾶ καὶ Ἀφροδίτη εὑρίσκουσι τὸ μῆλον καὶ φιλονεικοῦσαι ἔρχονται πρὸς τὸν Δία· αἷς αὐτὸς μὲν οὐκ ἔκρινεν, δι’ Ἑρμοῦ δὲ πρὸς τὸν ποιμένα Πάριν κριθησομένας περὶ κάλλους ἐξέπεμψεν. ἀλλ’ οὔτε ἐκρίθησαν θεαὶ οὔτε ὁ Πάρις τῇ Ἀφροδίτῃ τὸ μῆλον ἀπέδωκεν. οὐχ Ἀφροδίτη τιμηθεῖσα τῷ τῆς Ἑλένης αὐτὸν ἀντετίμησεν γάμῳ. οὐ γὰρ ἂν ἡ τῆς θεᾶς τιμὴ πρόφασις ἐγίνετο παμφύλου πολέμου καὶ ταῦτα ἐπ’ ὀλέθρῳ τοῦ τὴν τιμὴν ἀπειληφότος καὶ ἀγχιστεύοντος τῷ τῆς Ἀφροδίτης γένει. ἀλλὰ (ὡς ἔφην), ὦ τέκνον, ἔχει τινὰ λόγον τὰ τοιαῦτα οἰκεῖον καὶ φιλόσοφον, ἀλληγορίᾳ φρασθῆναι δυνάμενον, ὥστε σε ἀκούσαντα θαυμάσαι. κἀγὼ ἔφην Δέομαι μή με ἀναβαλλόμενος βασανίσῃς. καὶ ὃς ἔφη Μηδὲν φοβηθῇς· οὐ γὰρ ὑπερθήσομαι, ἀλλ’ ἄρξομαι ἤδη λέγειν.

ἦν ποτὲ ὅτε οὐδὲν ἦν πλὴν χάος καὶ στοιχείων ἀτάκτων ἔτι συντεφορημένων μίξις ἀδιάκριτος, τοῦτο καὶ τῆς φύσεως ὁμολογούσης καὶ τῶν μεγάλων ἀνδρῶν οὕτως ἔχειν νενοηκότων. καὶ μάρτυρα τῶν μεγάλων ἐν σοφίᾳ τὸν μέγιστον Ὅμηρον αὐτόν σοι παρέξομαι, εἰπόντα περὶ τῆς ἀνέκαθεν συγχύσεως ἀλλὰ ὑμεῖς μὲν πάντες ὕδωρ καὶ γαῖα γένοισθε, ὡς ἐκεῖθεν ἁπάντων τὴν γένεσιν ἐσχηκότων, καὶ μετὰ ἀνάλυσιν τῆς ὑγρᾶς καὶ γηίνης οὐσίας εἰς τὴν πρώτην πάλιν ἀποκαθισταμένων φύσιν, ὅ ἐστιν χάος. Ἡσίοδος δὲ ἐν τῇ θεογονίᾳ λέγει ἤτοι μὲν πρώτιστα χάος ἐγένετο. τὸ δὲ „ἐγένετο“ δῆλον ὅτι γεγενῆσθαι ὡς γενητὰ σημαίνει, οὐ τὸ ἀεὶ εἶναι ὡς ἀγένητα. καὶ Ὀρφεὺς δὲ τὸ χάος ὠῷ παρεικάζει, ἐν ᾧ τῶν πρώτων στοιχείων ἦν ἡ σύγχυσις. τοῦτο Ἡσίοδος χάος ὑποτίθεται, ὅπερ Ὀρφεὺς ὠὸν λέγει γενητόν, ἐξ ἀπείρου τῆς ὕλης προβεβλημένον, γεγονὸς δὲ οὕτω·

τῆς τετραγενοῦς ὕλης ἐμψύχου οὔσης καὶ ὅλου ἀπείρου τινὸς βυθοῦ ἀεὶ ῥέοντος καὶ ἀκρίτως φερομένου καὶ μυρίας ἀτελεῖς κράσεις ἄλλοτε ἄλλας ἐπαναγέοντος καὶ διὰ τοῦτο αὐτὰς ἀναλύοντος τῇ ἀταξίᾳ, καὶ κεχηνότος ὡς εἰς γένεσιν ζῴου δεθῆναι μὴ δυναμένου, συνέβη ποτέ, αὐτοῦ τοῦ ἀπείρου πελάγους ὑπὸ ἰδίας φύσεως περιωθουμένου, κινήσει φυσικῇ εὐτάκτως ῥυῆναι ἀπὸ τοῦ αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸ αὐτὸ ὥσπερ ἴλιγγα καὶ μίξαι τὰς οὐσίας, καὶ οὕτως ἐξ ἀκουστοῦ τῶν πάντων τὸ νοστιμώτατον, ὅπερ πρὸς γένεσιν ζῴου ἐπιτηδειότατον ἦν, ὥσπερ ἐν χώνῃ κατὰ μέσου ῥυῆναι τοῦ παντὸς καὶ ὑπὸ τῆς πάντα φερούσης ἴλιγγος χωρῆσαι εἰς βάθος καὶ τὸ περικείμενον πνεῦμα ἐπισπάσασθαι, καὶ ὡς εἰς γονιμώτατον συλληφθὲν ποιεῖν κριτικὴν σύστασιν. ὥσπερ γὰρ ἐν ὑγρῷ φιλεῖ γίνεσθαι πομφόλυξ, οὕτως σφαιροειδὲς πανταχόθεν συνελήφθη κύτος. ἔπειτα αὐτὸ ἐν ἑαυτῷ κυηθέν, ὑπὸ τοῦ παρειληφότος θειώδους πνεύματος ἀναφερόμενον, προέκυψεν εἰς φῶς μέγιστόν τι τοῦτο ἀποκύημα, ὡς ἂν ἐκ παντὸς τοῦ ἀπείρου βυθοῦ ἀποκεκυημένον ἔμψυχον δημιούργημα καὶ τῇ περιφερείᾳ τῶν ὠῶν προσεοικὸς καὶ τῷ τάχει τῆς πτήσεως.

Κρόνον οὖν τὸν χρόνον μοι νόει, τὴν δὲ Ῥέαν τὸ ῥέον τῆς ὑγρᾶς οὐσίας, ὅτι χρόνῳ φερομένη ἡ ὕλη ἅπασα ὥσπερ ὠὸν τὸν πάντα περιέχοντα σφαιροειδῆ ἀπεκύησεν οὐρανόν· ὅπερ κατ’ ἀρχὰς τοῦ γονίμου μυελοῦ πλῆρες ἦν ὡς ἂν στοιχεῖα καὶ χρώματα παντοδαπὰ ἐκτεκεῖν δυνάμενον, καὶ ὅμως παντοδαπὴν ἐκ μιᾶς οὐσίας τε καὶ χρώματος ἑνὸς ἔφερε τὴν φαντασίαν. ὥσπερ γὰρ ἐν τῷ τοῦ ταῶ γεννήματι ἓν μὲν τοῦ ὠοῦ χρῶμα δοκεῖ, δυνάμει δὲ μυρία ἔχει ἐν ἑαυτῷ τοῦ μέλλοντος τελεσφορεῖσθαι χρώματα, οὕτως καὶ τὸ ἐξ ἀπείρου ὕλης ἀποκυηθὲν ἔμψυχον ὠὸν ἐκ τῆς ὑποκειμένης καὶ ἀεὶ ῥεούσης ὕλης κινούμενον παντοδαπὰς ἐκφαίνει τροπάς. ἔνδοθεν γὰρ τῆς περιφερείας ζῷόν τι ἀρρενόθηλυ εἰδοποιεῖται προνοίᾳ τοῦ ἐνόντος ἐν αὐτῷ θείου πνεύματος, ὃν Φάνητα Ὀρφεὺς καλεῖ, ὅτι αὐτοῦ φανέντος τὸ πᾶν ἐξ αὐτοῦ ἔλαμψεν, τῷ φέγγει τοῦ διαπρεπεστάτου τῶν στοιχείων πυρὸς ἐν τῷ ὑγρῷ τελεσφορουμένου. καὶ οὐκ ἄπιστον, ὅτι καὶ ἐπὶ λαμπυρίδων δείγματος ἕνεκα ἡ φύσις ἡμῖν ὁρᾶν ὑγρὸν φῶς ἐδωρήσατο.

context.translation_policy_text:
# Translation Stance

This document states the translation commitments that guide every
decision in the People's Open Bible. Declaring them is an act of
honesty: critics can assess our output against our stated
commitments rather than guessing at hidden biases.

> **Status: first draft.** This document will be refined as the
> project matures. Input and disagreement are welcomed via GitHub
> issues.

## Theological stance

The People's Open Bible does not commit to a specific denominational
or creedal doctrinal stance. Where the source texts presuppose
theological claims — the divinity of Christ, the resurrection,
the personhood of the Holy Spirit, the unity of God — the
translation reflects those claims as the texts present them, not
as imposed commitments of the translator.

Readers from any tradition (Catholic, Eastern Orthodox, Protestant
of any stripe, non-denominational, inquirer) are invited to
evaluate POB against their own framework. Where a translation
decision is influenced by a theological reading — for example,
where a Greek construction is genuinely ambiguous and the English
choice leans one way or the other — that choice is documented in
the verse's `theological_decisions` block and the alternative
rendering is preserved in a footnote.

We do not pick sides on denominational distinctives (Reformed vs.
Arminian, infant vs. believer's baptism, real presence vs.
symbolic, cessationist vs. continuationist, etc.). Those questions
are for the reader and their faith community, not for the
translation.

## Translation philosophy

The People's Open Bible aims at **optimal equivalence**: the most faithful,
intelligible English representation of the source's meaning, wording patterns,
literary form, and rhetorical force. This is not an automatic midpoint between
formal and dynamic translation. Readability serves source fidelity; convention
and familiarity do not override it.

Specifically:

1. **Original-language primacy with reader-conscious wording.** Where
   long-standing English renderings obscure the source text's plain
   sense, we explain the source pressure openly. For *doulos*, the main
   text uses "servant" consistently while notes and the public audit
   trail preserve bonded-status, ownership, and total-allegiance nuance
   where it is historically or theologically salient (Rom 1:1, Phil 1:1).

2. **Translate titles; use conventional name forms.** Christological
   titles are translated to preserve meaning (*Christos* →
   "Messiah" when it functions independently as a title; *Kyrios* →
   "Lord"). In name-like constructions, use the familiar English forms
   "Jesus Christ" and "Christ Jesus." Personal names are otherwise
   transliterated by standard conventions. Thus "Jesus is the Messiah"
   retains the title, while Greek *Iēsous Christos* used as a personal-name
   construction is rendered "Jesus Christ."

3. **Preserve theological tension rather than resolve it.** Where
   the source is genuinely ambiguous on a contested interpretive
   question (e.g., *pistis Christou* — "faith in Christ" vs.
   "faithfulness of Christ"), we render one in the main text and
   preserve the alternative in a footnote, documenting the
   decision in the per-verse YAML.

4. **Consistency of key terms, or documented exception.** A given
   Greek or Hebrew word should receive a consistent English gloss
   across the translation, unless context demands variance — in
   which case the variance is documented per-verse with a
   rationale. The `consistency_lint.py` tool enforces this at
   commit time.

5. **Readable modern English, not archaic or academic.** The
   target reader is a literate 18–35-year-old English speaker.
   Vocabulary should be accessible without flattening theological
   weight. We avoid both ecclesiastical jargon ("propitiation" is
   footnoted, not required) and informality that undersells the
   text's gravity.

## Source distinctions and optimal English

Source fidelity takes priority over mere familiarity or defensibility. A
significant Greek or Hebrew wording pattern must receive an explicit comparison
with the best source-transparent English candidate, even when a prior draft
already discusses it in a footnote. Prior rationale is evidence, not a veto.
Do not infer different meanings from morphology alone or invent theology to
justify different glosses; preserve observable wording without adding claims.
A concise source-qualified or hyphenated rendering is available when ordinary
English otherwise conceals the source pattern. Record unresolved proposals for
maintainer review; do not silently certify them as unchanged or auto-publish.

**Approved scoped rendering:** John 21:15–17 uses **agape-love** for ἀγαπάω
and **phileo-love** for φιλέω, including the repeated question in verse 17.
The ἀγάπη noun's general table entry below is not a rule erasing that verb
pattern. Do not revert this approved POB/SPOB wording to generic “love”.

## Contested terms

The following terms appear frequently and carry heavy theological
weight. Our default rendering and rationale are recorded here.
Per-verse variance is documented in the individual YAML files.

| Greek / Hebrew | Default English | Alternatives considered | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| Χριστός *Christos* | Messiah where independently titular; Christ in the name forms "Jesus Christ" / "Christ Jesus" | Christ, Messiah | Preserves the title's Hebraic messianic meaning while using the recognizable conventional English personal name |
| κύριος *Kyrios* | Lord | LORD, Master | Matches covenantal and NT usage |
| δοῦλος *doulos* | servant | bondservant, slave | Uses reader-facing "servant" consistently; documents bonded-status and ownership nuance in notes/audit metadata |
| πίστις *pistis* | faith | faithfulness, trust | Main text: faith; footnote alternatives where contested |
| δικαιοσύνη *dikaiosynē* | righteousness | justice | Both renderings preserved in footnotes for Pauline passages |
| ἱλαστήριον *hilastērion* | atoning sacrifice | propitiation, mercy seat | Dynamic rendering for accessibility; alternatives footnoted |
| ἀγάπη *agapē* | love | charity (archaic) | Lexical cognates in source kept |
| σάρξ *sarx* | flesh (literal) / sinful nature (metaphorical) | — | Context-dependent; per-verse documented |
| μετανοέω / μετάνοια *metanoeō / metanoia* | reorient / reorientation; toward God where the context warrants making the destination explicit | repent / repentance (traditional); reconsider / change of mind in documented exceptions | See "Reorientation terminology (2026-10-11)" below; do not homogenize regret, divine relenting, or distinct turning words |
| νήφω *nēphō* | clear-minded (most contexts); sober (where Paul explicitly runs the drunk/sober metaphor) | sober-minded | See revision notes in 1 Pet 5:8, 1 Thess 5:6 |
| יְהוָה YHWH | Yahweh | the LORD, Jehovah | Renders the divine name as a name. Where the NT quotes an OT YHWH passage using *Kyrios*, the NT verse retains "Lord" to preserve the Greek; the OT source verse uses "Yahweh". |
| אָדָם *adam* | man / humankind (context) | — | Context-dependent per usage |

## Reorientation terminology (2026-10-11)

Maintainer-approved English POB and SPOB reader wording uses **reorient /
reorientation** in place of the repent family for moral-spiritual redirection.
Use **toward God** when the context warrants making that direction explicit;
use **toward you** in direct prayer, and omit the extra destination when the
sentence already names it, supplies a departure from wrongdoing, or concerns
interpersonal reconsideration. Acts 20:21 explicitly supplies the Godward
phrase. The word *metanoia* by itself does not lexically contain "God."

This is an English editorial policy, not a claim that remorse is irrelevant or
that Greek word parts establish the full meaning. Preserve sorrow, named sins,
faith, forgiveness, and the distinction between a response and its fruit.
Keep separate turning expressions in Acts 3:19 and 26:20. Baptism's relationship
to reorientation must not be rewritten as "only symbolizes" or "causes."

**Context controls exceptions.** Retain regret, relenting, reconsideration,
change of mind, or turning back where that is the supported sense. Do not make
God reorient toward God; do not make a persecutor's demand for apostasy a call
toward God. Preserve contested interpretations in Job 42:6 and Hebrews 12:17.
Extra-canonical authors retain their own conceptual frameworks. Adapting a
historical English witness is not a new ancient-language translation, and must
be disclosed while its source transcription remains untouched.

**No invented intensifiers.** Do not add "fully," "completely," "radically,"
"truly," "wholeheartedly," or a superlative simply to strengthen reorientation.
Preserve such force only where the source supplies it. Hermas V.3.xiii.4
(reader chapter 21:4) has *holotelōs* and *ex holēs kardias*; its existing
"completely" and "from their whole heart" are not new additions.

Traditional terminology remains in alternative notes, original sources, and
historical revision records. Do not rewrite those layers to manufacture a
history of agreement. See [the application report](docs/REORIENTATION_POLICY_2026-10-11.md)
and the hash-bound plan in `config/terminology/`.

## What the translation is not

To prevent misunderstanding:

- **Not a paraphrase.** Every English rendering is tied to a
  specific source-text word or phrase, documented in the per-verse
  YAML.
- **Not a study Bible.** Footnotes document translation decisions,
  not doctrinal application or devotional commentary.
- **Not a denominational product.** The translation is
  intentionally cross-denominational. Contested readings are
  preserved in footnotes, not smoothed away.
- **Not a finalized translation.** Every verse is currently an
  AI-drafted rendering, released openly with full rationale. There
  is no formal scholarly review process at this time.
- **Not a first-century English approximation.** We aim at modern
  English that honors source-language meaning, not at archaism.

## Translating into other languages

The People's Open Bible's long-term intention is to be translated
into every major world language. Scripture belongs to the whole
church; producing POB only in English would contradict the
project's mission.

Each target language is its own translation — drafted directly
from the original-language sources (Hebrew OT, Greek NT, Swete
LXX for the deuterocanonical books) rather than from the English
POB. Translating from English would compound the distance from the
originals and inherit choices that make sense in English but not
elsewhere. Every target language deserves its own encounter with
the Hebrew and Greek.

Each language goes through **several revision passes** before it
is considered stable:

1. **AI-drafted first pass** — a frontier multilingual model
   produces the initial verse-by-verse draft with full per-verse
   provenance, following the same methodology used for English
   (DOCTRINE.md translation philosophy §§1–5, per-verse YAML
   schema, `doctrine_reference` citations where relevant).
2. **AI-reviewer revision** — a second, distinct model reads the
   draft and flags awkward phrasing, dropped nuance, or places
   where the target language's idiom has drifted from the
   source's force. Revisions are discrete commits.
3. **Native-speaker community review** — before a language is
   declared stable, speakers of that language who are also
   familiar with the biblical source languages (or who have
   access to published lexicons in that language) audit the
   text and raise issues publicly.
4. **Public issue window** — a minimum public-review period with
   open GitHub issues before any language moves from "preview"
   to "stable."

**Supported languages will be disclosed publicly based on model
performance and feasibility.** Not every language has an AI model
capable of scholarly-accurate translation yet, and not every
language has a sufficient community of native-speaking reviewers
accessible to the project. We will publish the current supported-
language list, and the ready-but-not-yet-stable list, as we reach
the capability threshold for each. Languages that do not yet meet
the bar are named as such, not silently omitted.

Every language published under this program carries the same
CC-BY 4.0 license, the same per-verse provenance, the same
auditability. There is no tier system across languages — every
supported language gets the full People's Open Bible.

## Change log for this document

Material changes to this document are themselves commits. Prior
versions of the stance are preserved in git history.

- **2026-04-21:** Removed creedal affirmations (Apostles' Creed,
  Nicene Creed, Chalcedonian Definition) and replaced with a
  theological-stance section that declines specific creedal
  commitment. Translation philosophy and contested-terms table
  preserved unchanged; those are methodology, not creedal
  commitment, and the project actually runs on them. Added a
  "Translating into other languages" section stating POB's long-
  term intention to ship in every feasible major language, with
  the full revision pipeline and transparent supported-language
  disclosure. Per-verse YAML citing the old `doctrine_reference`
  values is preserved as historical record; those are not
  retroactively edited.
context.ambiguity_review_standard: Apply the supplied DOCTRINE.md ambiguity policy: a defensible contextual rendering may be used in the main text when material alternatives and the reason for the choice are preserved in notes. A unique or uncontested interpretation is not required. Distinguish (a) an unreadable or unverified source, omitted content, invented restoration, or a construction for which no defensible English can be given, from (b) ordinary lexical, attachment, or referent ambiguity faithfully preserved in English or explained with viable alternatives. The former blocks publication; the latter does not automatically block it. A note cannot excuse unsupported wording: the proposed main rendering must itself be defensible from the supplied Greek. Clearly printed gaps must remain gaps, not be filled by invention. Never change a verdict merely to achieve acceptance.

passages.text: On the third day I went with my closest companions to the appointed place in Tyre. There I found Apion sitting between Anubion and Athenodorus, waiting for us with many other educated men. Nevertheless, I was not at all intimidated. I greeted him and sat down opposite Apion, who soon began to speak: ‘I want to begin first and move quickly from here to the question at issue. Before you joined us, my child Clement, this Anubion and Athenodorus, who heard you speaking yesterday along with the others, told me how, when I associated with you in Rome on the assumption that you were in love, I told many lies about the gods. I said they were lovers of boys, sexually unrestrained, having relations with mothers, sisters, and daughters, and involved in countless adulteries. But you should have known, my child, that I did not write these things because I held such views about the gods. Rather, out of affection for you, I held back from telling the truth. If you now wish, hear that truth from me.’

lexical_decisions.chosen: on the assumption that you were in love
lexical_decisions.rationale: The dative participle refers to Clement, with whom Apion associated. The phrase presents the supposition under which Apion acted; it does not name the object of Clement's supposed love. ‘As with someone in love’ is a closer but less natural alternative.

lexical_decisions.chosen: lovers of boys, sexually unrestrained
lexical_decisions.rationale: The first term names the gods' alleged sexual interest in boys, and the second their lack of sexual restraint in this context. The rendering preserves the historical accusation without adding details.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: στοργῇ τῇ πρὸς σὲ τὰ ἀληθῆ λέγειν ἀπεκρυπτόμην
lexical_decisions.chosen: out of affection for you, I held back from telling the truth
lexical_decisions.rationale: The middle verb and infinitive express Apion's concealment or withholding of his truthful account. ‘I concealed the truth from you out of affection’ is also possible, but loses the explicit reference to speaking.

source_issues.issue: The first occurrence spells Anubion's name with doubled nu, while the same passage later has Ἀνουβίων. The English uses the conventional name Anubion for both occurrences; no second person is inferred.

passages.text: ‘The wisest men of old learned the whole truth themselves through hard work, but kept those who were unworthy and had no desire for divine teachings from receiving this knowledge. For twelve children were not born to Uranus and his mother Earth, as the myth lists them: the males Oceanus, Coeus, Crius, Hyperion, Iapetus, and Cronus; and the females Theia, Themis, Mnemosyne, Demeter, Tethys, and Rhea. Nor did Cronus cut off the genitals of his father Uranus with an adamantine sickle, as you say, and throw them into the depths. Nor did Aphrodite come into being from drops of blood that flowed from Uranus's severed part. Nor, again, did Cronus have relations with Rhea and, after fathering Pluto first, swallow him, fearing because of some pronouncement of Prometheus that a child born to him might prove nobler than he was and strip him of his kingship. He did not father Poseidon second and swallow him in the same way. After these, when Zeus was born, his mother Rhea did not hide him and give Cronus a stone instead when he demanded him to swallow. That stone did not, when swallowed, squeeze those swallowed earlier and force them out, so that Pluto, the first swallowed, came out first, Poseidon after him, and Zeus third. Nor, as they say, did Zeus, saved by his mother's foresight, ascend into heaven and depose his father from his kingship. He did not punish his father's brothers. He did not come down out of desire for mortal women. He did not have shameful relations with sisters or daughters, with brothers' wives, or with boys. Nor did he beget Metis and swallow her ...., so that he might cause Athena from Metis to grow out of his brain and give birth from his thigh to Dionysus, whom they say the Titans tore apart. He does not hold a feast at the wedding of Thetis and Peleus. He did not exclude Strife from the wedding. This Strife, dishonored, did not devise conflict and faction among the guests. She did not take a golden apple from the gardens of the Hesperides and inscribe on it, “A gift for the beautiful one.” Then they tell the myth that Hera, Athena, and Aphrodite find the apple and, quarreling over it, come to Zeus. He did not judge between them himself, but sent them through Hermes to the shepherd Paris to have their beauty judged. Yet the goddesses were not judged, nor did Paris award the apple to Aphrodite. Aphrodite, thus honored, did not honor him in return with marriage to Helen. For the goddess's honor would not have become the occasion for a war involving every people, and that to the destruction of the man who had received the honor and was closely related to Aphrodite's family. But, as I said, my child, such stories have an appropriate philosophical explanation, capable of being expressed through allegory, so that you will marvel when you hear it.’ I said, ‘Please do not torment me by delaying.’ He replied, ‘Have no fear. I will not put it off, but will begin speaking now.’

lexical_decisions.chosen: with an adamantine sickle
lexical_decisions.rationale: Adamant names the exceptionally hard material of the mythic weapon. ‘A sickle of adamant’ is equally close; specifying steel or diamond would identify a material more precisely than the Greek warrants.

lexical_decisions.chosen: because of some pronouncement of Prometheus
lexical_decisions.rationale: The noun can denote an ordinance or decree, here a pronouncement that supplies the reason for Cronus's fear. ‘Decree’ preserves its authoritative force more explicitly; ‘prophecy’ fits the story but narrows the noun beyond what is stated.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὃς οὐ καταποθεὶς τοὺς προκαταποθέντας θλίψας ἐξῶσεν
lexical_decisions.chosen: That stone did not, when swallowed, squeeze those swallowed earlier and force them out
lexical_decisions.rationale: The negative is taken with the finite verb, within Apion's repeated denials of mythic events, rather than as ‘not swallowed’ attached only to the participle. The swallowed participle and the stone as subject are both retained.

lexical_decisions.chosen: Nor did he beget Metis and swallow her
lexical_decisions.rationale: The supplied active participle says ‘having begotten,’ with Metis as its expressed object. The translation preserves that wording rather than substituting a familiar myth about impregnation or swallowing an already pregnant Metis.

lexical_decisions.chosen: A gift for the beautiful one
lexical_decisions.rationale: The adjective is positive, not superlative. ‘For the fairest’ would introduce a degree not expressed in this wording.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: λόγον τὰ τοιαῦτα οἰκεῖον καὶ φιλόσοφον, ἀλληγορίᾳ φρασθῆναι δυνάμενον
lexical_decisions.chosen: such stories have an appropriate philosophical explanation, capable of being expressed through allegory
lexical_decisions.rationale: The account is both fitting to its subject and philosophical, and allegory is the means of expressing it. ‘An explanation proper to them and philosophical in character’ is more explicit but heavier English.

source_issues.issue: The selected edition prints a gap of four dots after ‘swallowed.’ The English retains exactly four dots at the corresponding point. Its unavailable content has not been restored, and the sentence must not be represented as an unbroken original.

source_issues.source_quote: ὡς προελθεῖν πρῶτον μὲν τὸν πρῶτον καταποθέντα Πλούτωνα, ἐπ’ αὐτῷ δὲ Ποσειδῶνα καὶ τρίτον τὸν Δία
source_issues.issue: This enumeration includes Zeus third among those coming out, although the preceding account has Rhea hide him. The translation retains the supplied names and order instead of reconciling the narrative with itself or with other versions of the myth.

passages.text: ‘There was once a time when nothing existed except chaos and an undifferentiated mixture of elements still heaped together without order. Nature itself acknowledges this, and great men have understood that this was so. I will give you Homer himself as a witness, the greatest in wisdom among great men. Speaking of the original confusion, he says, “But may you all become water and earth,” since everything originated from that state and, after the dissolution of its moist and earthy substance, is restored again to its first nature, which is chaos. Hesiod says in his Theogony, “Indeed, first of all chaos came into being.” Clearly, “came into being” signifies having originated, as things that come into being do, not always existing, as things without origin do. Orpheus, too, compares chaos to an egg, in which the first elements were mixed together. What Hesiod proposes as chaos, Orpheus calls an egg that came into being, brought forth from boundless matter. It came about in this way:’

lexical_decisions.source_quote: χάος καὶ στοιχείων ἀτάκτων ἔτι συντεφορημένων μίξις ἀδιάκριτος
lexical_decisions.chosen: chaos and an undifferentiated mixture of elements still heaped together without order
lexical_decisions.rationale: The rendering retains both the named chaos and the description of the mixture, including the elements' disorder and lack of differentiation. ‘An unseparated mixture’ is another possible rendering of the last adjective.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: γεγενῆσθαι ὡς γενητὰ σημαίνει, οὐ τὸ ἀεὶ εἶναι ὡς ἀγένητα
lexical_decisions.chosen: signifies having originated, as things that come into being do, not always existing, as things without origin do
lexical_decisions.rationale: The distinction concerns coming into existence versus existing without an origin. ‘Created’ and ‘uncreated’ could introduce a maker not specified in these terms; ‘begotten’ could imply biological generation too narrowly.

lexical_decisions.chosen: brought forth from boundless matter
lexical_decisions.rationale: The verb describes the egg's being projected or brought forth, while the adjective qualifies matter as unlimited. The translation does not identify a personal agent where none is supplied.

passages.text: ‘The fourfold matter was alive, and an entire boundless deep was forever flowing and moving without differentiation, bringing up countless incomplete mixtures, now one and now another, and so dissolving them in its disorder. It gaped open, unable to be bound together so as to generate a living being. At some point, as the boundless sea itself was driven around by its own nature, it happened to flow in an orderly way, by a natural movement, from the same point back to that same point, like a whirlpool, and to mix the substances. Thus, from what was audible, the richest part of everything, which was particularly suited to generating a living being, flowed through the middle of the whole as through a funnel. Driven by the whirlpool that carried everything, it moved into the depths and drew in the surrounding breath; and, gathered together into a supremely fertile state, it formed a structure capable of differentiation. For just as a bubble tends to form in liquid, so a spherical cavity took shape, enclosed on every side. Then, having developed within itself and being lifted by the sulfurous breath it had taken in, this enormous offspring emerged into the light: a living work brought forth, as it were, from the entire boundless deep, resembling eggs in its round shape and in the speed of its flight.’

lexical_decisions.chosen: The fourfold matter was alive
lexical_decisions.rationale: The matter comprises four kinds and is described as possessing life or soul. ‘The matter of four kinds was ensouled’ is more technical; ‘alive’ keeps the assertion accessible without replacing it with a modern physical explanation.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐξ ἀκουστοῦ τῶν πάντων τὸ νοστιμώτατον
lexical_decisions.chosen: from what was audible, the richest part of everything
lexical_decisions.rationale: The supplied ἀκουστοῦ is rendered according to its ordinary sense ‘audible’ or ‘heard’; the resulting unusual phrase is not silently changed to ‘from it’ or a different cosmological expression. The superlative νοστιμώτατον is read as the choicest or richest portion, clarified by the following statement of its suitability for generating life. See the separate source issue.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὡς εἰς γονιμώτατον συλληφθὲν ποιεῖν κριτικὴν σύστασιν
lexical_decisions.chosen: gathered together into a supremely fertile state, it formed a structure capable of differentiation
lexical_decisions.rationale: The wording combines gathering or conception with a superlatively generative condition and a κριτική constitution. ‘A discerning constitution’ is a material alternative if the adjective points to a living being's discriminating faculty rather than physical differentiation. The main rendering preserves the capacity to distinguish without importing a specific physiological mechanism.

lexical_decisions.chosen: a spherical cavity took shape, enclosed on every side
lexical_decisions.rationale: Κύτος can denote a hollow container, cavity, or enclosing body; the bubble analogy favors a cavity enclosed on all sides. The translation does not identify a shell material.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the sulfurous breath it had taken in
lexical_decisions.rationale: Θειώδης can mean sulfurous, while divine-like is a material alternative from the related divine vocabulary; the physical account of the rising enclosed breath supports sulfurous here. Πνεῦμα is rendered breath in this physical account, though wind or spirit are possible. The following section's explicit θεῖον πνεῦμα is separately rendered divine spirit rather than automatically homogenized with this adjective.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῇ περιφερείᾳ τῶν ὠῶν προσεοικὸς καὶ τῷ τάχει τῆς πτήσεως
lexical_decisions.chosen: resembling eggs in its round shape and in the speed of its flight
lexical_decisions.rationale: Both coordinated respects of resemblance are retained. The unusual reference to an egg's flight is not removed, explained by an invented mechanism, or silently reassigned to another comparison.

source_issues.issue: The supplied wording literally supports ‘from what was audible’ or ‘from what was heard,’ but its role in this physical account is obscure. The English retains the audible sense openly rather than conjecturally replacing the printed Greek. This is not a claim that the cosmological referent has been identified; no alternative source wording has been supplied.

The reference to speed of flight is grammatically coordinated with roundness in the egg comparison, but the physical sense is unusual. Both surviving expressions are translated without supplying an absent explanation.

passages.text: ‘Understand Cronus, then, as time, and Rhea as the flowing of moist substance, because all matter, carried along in time, gave birth, like an egg, to the spherical heaven that contains everything. At first this was full of generative marrow, capable of producing elements and colors of every kind. Yet from one substance and a single color it presented an appearance of every kind. For just as in the offspring of a peacock the egg appears to have one color, but potentially contains within itself the countless colors of the creature that will reach full development, so the living egg brought forth from boundless matter, moved by the underlying, ever-flowing matter, reveals changes of every kind. For within its circumference a male-and-female living being takes shape through the providence of the divine spirit present in it. Orpheus calls him Phanes, because, when he appeared, the whole universe shone from him through the brilliance of fire, the most radiant of the elements, which reached full development in the moisture. This is not unbelievable, since nature has also granted us a sight of moist light in glowworms as an example.’

lexical_decisions.source_quote: Κρόνον οὖν τὸν χρόνον μοι νόει, τὴν δὲ Ῥέαν τὸ ῥέον τῆς ὑγρᾶς οὐσίας
lexical_decisions.chosen: Understand Cronus, then, as time, and Rhea as the flowing of moist substance
lexical_decisions.rationale: The allegory associates Cronus with χρόνος, time, and Rhea with ῥέον, flowing. The English translates the explanations while retaining the names; their Greek sound associations cannot be fully reproduced in English.

lexical_decisions.chosen: generative marrow
lexical_decisions.rationale: The bodily term marrow and its life-producing quality are both preserved. ‘Fertile core’ would be smoother but would obscure the explicit bodily image.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: παντοδαπὴν ἐκ μιᾶς οὐσίας τε καὶ χρώματος ἑνὸς ἔφερε τὴν φαντασίαν
lexical_decisions.chosen: from one substance and a single color it presented an appearance of every kind
lexical_decisions.rationale: The rendering keeps the contrast between the single substance and color and the manifold appearance. ‘A variegated appearance’ is more idiomatic but could make the statement concern visible colors alone, while the next comparison expressly distinguishes visible color from potential colors.

lexical_decisions.chosen: a male-and-female living being takes shape
lexical_decisions.rationale: The compound describes one living being as both male and female. It does not describe two separate creatures or introduce a modern identity category.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: Φάνητα Ὀρφεὺς καλεῖ, ὅτι αὐτοῦ φανέντος τὸ πᾶν ἐξ αὐτοῦ ἔλαμψεν
lexical_decisions.chosen: Orpheus calls him Phanes, because, when he appeared, the whole universe shone from him
lexical_decisions.rationale: The conventional name Phanes is retained, with the source's explanatory connection to appearing and shining. The explanation is the speaker's ancient account, not a claim of established etymology.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῷ φέγγει τοῦ διαπρεπεστάτου τῶν στοιχείων πυρὸς ἐν τῷ ὑγρῷ τελεσφορουμένου
lexical_decisions.chosen: through the brilliance of fire, the most radiant of the elements, which reached full development in the moisture
lexical_decisions.rationale: The genitive participle agrees with fire, so its reaching full development in moisture is retained. The superlative explicitly supports ‘most radiant’; the translation does not attribute the development only to light.

lexical_decisions.chosen: in glowworms as an example
lexical_decisions.rationale: The noun denotes luminous insects. ‘Fireflies’ is a viable familiar alternative; the Greek does not specify a modern species.

τὸ μὲν οὖν πρωτοσύστατον ὠὸν ὑποθερμανθὲν ὑπὸ τοῦ ἔσωθεν ζῴου ῥήγνυται, ἔπειτα δὲ μορφωθὲν προέρχεται ὁποῖόν τι καὶ Ὀρφεὺς λέγει, κραναίου σχισθέντος πολυχανδέος ὠοῦ. καὶ οὕτω μεγάλῃ δυνάμει αὐτοῦ τοῦ προεληλυθότος φανέντος, τὸ μὲν κύτος τὴν ἁρμονίαν λαμβάνει καὶ τὴν διακόσμησιν ἴσχει, αὐτὸς δὲ ὥσπερ ἐπ’ ἀκρωρείας οὐρανοῦ προκαθέζεται, καὶ ἐν ἀπορρήτοις τὸν ἄπειρον περιλάμπων αἰῶνα. ἡ δὲ τοῦ κύτους ἔνδοθεν γόνιμος ὑπολειφθεῖσα ὕλη, ὡς ἐν πολλῷ τῷ χρόνῳ ὑποκειμένης ἕως φυσικῆς ὑποζέουσα ἡ θερμότης, τὰς πάντων διέκρινεν οὐσίας. τὸ μὲν γὰρ κατώτερον αὐτῆς πρῶτον ὥσπερ ὑποστάθμη ὑπὸ τοῦ βάρους εἰς τὰ κάτω ὑποκεχώρηκεν, ὃ διὰ τὴν ὁλκότητα καὶ διὰ τὸ ἐμβριθὲς καὶ πολὺ τῆς ὑποκειμένης οὐσίας πλῆθος Πλούτωνα προσηγόρευσαν, ᾅδου τε καὶ νεκρῶν βασιλέα εἶναι ἀποφηνάμενοι.

## Theological stance

The People's Open Bible does not commit to a specific denominational
or creedal doctrinal stance. Where the source texts presuppose
theological claims — the divinity of Christ, the resurrection,
the personhood of the Holy Spirit, the unity of God — the
translation reflects those claims as the texts present them, not
as imposed commitments of the translator.

Readers from any tradition (Catholic, Eastern Orthodox, Protestant
of any stripe, non-denominational, inquirer) are invited to
evaluate POB against their own framework. Where a translation
decision is influenced by a theological reading — for example,
where a Greek construction is genuinely ambiguous and the English
choice leans one way or the other — that choice is documented in
the verse's `theological_decisions` block and the alternative
rendering is preserved in a footnote.

We do not pick sides on denominational distinctives (Reformed vs.
Arminian, infant vs. believer's baptism, real presence vs.
symbolic, cessationist vs. continuationist, etc.). Those questions
are for the reader and their faith community, not for the
translation.

## Translation philosophy

The People's Open Bible aims at **optimal equivalence**: the most faithful,
intelligible English representation of the source's meaning, wording patterns,
literary form, and rhetorical force. This is not an automatic midpoint between
formal and dynamic translation. Readability serves source fidelity; convention
and familiarity do not override it.

Specifically:

1. **Original-language primacy with reader-conscious wording.** Where
   long-standing English renderings obscure the source text's plain
   sense, we explain the source pressure openly. For *doulos*, the main
   text uses "servant" consistently while notes and the public audit
   trail preserve bonded-status, ownership, and total-allegiance nuance
   where it is historically or theologically salient (Rom 1:1, Phil 1:1).

2. **Translate titles; use conventional name forms.** Christological
   titles are translated to preserve meaning (*Christos* →
   "Messiah" when it functions independently as a title; *Kyrios* →
   "Lord"). In name-like constructions, use the familiar English forms
   "Jesus Christ" and "Christ Jesus." Personal names are otherwise
   transliterated by standard conventions. Thus "Jesus is the Messiah"
   retains the title, while Greek *Iēsous Christos* used as a personal-name
   construction is rendered "Jesus Christ."

3. **Preserve theological tension rather than resolve it.** Where
   the source is genuinely ambiguous on a contested interpretive
   question (e.g., *pistis Christou* — "faith in Christ" vs.
   "faithfulness of Christ"), we render one in the main text and
   preserve the alternative in a footnote, documenting the
   decision in the per-verse YAML.

4. **Consistency of key terms, or documented exception.** A given
   Greek or Hebrew word should receive a consistent English gloss
   across the translation, unless context demands variance — in
   which case the variance is documented per-verse with a
   rationale. The `consistency_lint.py` tool enforces this at
   commit time.

5. **Readable modern English, not archaic or academic.** The
   target reader is a literate 18–35-year-old English speaker.
   Vocabulary should be accessible without flattening theological
   weight. We avoid both ecclesiastical jargon ("propitiation" is
   footnoted, not required) and informality that undersells the
   text's gravity.

## Source distinctions and optimal English

Source fidelity takes priority over mere familiarity or defensibility. A
significant Greek or Hebrew wording pattern must receive an explicit comparison
with the best source-transparent English candidate, even when a prior draft
already discusses it in a footnote. Prior rationale is evidence, not a veto.
Do not infer different meanings from morphology alone or invent theology to
justify different glosses; preserve observable wording without adding claims.
A concise source-qualified or hyphenated rendering is available when ordinary
English otherwise conceals the source pattern. Record unresolved proposals for
maintainer review; do not silently certify them as unchanged or auto-publish.

## Reorientation terminology (2026-10-11)

Maintainer-approved English POB and SPOB reader wording uses **reorient /
reorientation** in place of the repent family for moral-spiritual redirection.
Use **toward God** when the context warrants making that direction explicit;
use **toward you** in direct prayer, and omit the extra destination when the
sentence already names it, supplies a departure from wrongdoing, or concerns
interpersonal reconsideration. Acts 20:21 explicitly supplies the Godward
phrase. The word *metanoia* by itself does not lexically contain "God."

This is an English editorial policy, not a claim that remorse is irrelevant or
that Greek word parts establish the full meaning. Preserve sorrow, named sins,
faith, forgiveness, and the distinction between a response and its fruit.
Keep separate turning expressions in Acts 3:19 and 26:20. Baptism's relationship
to reorientation must not be rewritten as "only symbolizes" or "causes."

**Context controls exceptions.** Retain regret, relenting, reconsideration,
change of mind, or turning back where that is the supported sense. Do not make
God reorient toward God; do not make a persecutor's demand for apostasy a call
toward God. Preserve contested interpretations in Job 42:6 and Hebrews 12:17.
Extra-canonical authors retain their own conceptual frameworks. Adapting a
historical English witness is not a new ancient-language translation, and must
be disclosed while its source transcription remains untouched.

**No invented intensifiers.** Do not add "fully," "completely," "radically,"
"truly," "wholeheartedly," or a superlative simply to strengthen reorientation.
Preserve such force only where the source supplies it. Hermas V.3.xiii.4
(reader chapter 21:4) has *holotelōs* and *ex holēs kardias*; its existing
"completely" and "from their whole heart" are not new additions.

Traditional terminology remains in alternative notes, original sources, and
historical revision records. Do not rewrite those layers to manufacture a
history of agreement. See [the application report](docs/REORIENTATION_POLICY_2026-10-11.md)
and the hash-bound plan in `config/terminology/`.

## What the translation is not

To prevent misunderstanding:

- **Not a paraphrase.** Every English rendering is tied to a
  specific source-text word or phrase, documented in the per-verse
  YAML.
- **Not a study Bible.** Footnotes document translation decisions,
  not doctrinal application or devotional commentary.
- **Not a denominational product.** The translation is
  intentionally cross-denominational. Contested readings are
  preserved in footnotes, not smoothed away.
- **Not a finalized translation.** Every verse is currently an
  AI-drafted rendering, released openly with full rationale. There
  is no formal scholarly review process at this time.
- **Not a first-century English approximation.** We aim at modern
  English that honors source-language meaning, not at archaism.

## Translating into other languages

The People's Open Bible's long-term intention is to be translated
into every major world language. Scripture belongs to the whole
church; producing POB only in English would contradict the
project's mission.

Each target language is its own translation — drafted directly
from the original-language sources (Hebrew OT, Greek NT, Swete
LXX for the deuterocanonical books) rather than from the English
POB. Translating from English would compound the distance from the
originals and inherit choices that make sense in English but not
elsewhere. Every target language deserves its own encounter with
the Hebrew and Greek.

Each language goes through **several revision passes** before it
is considered stable:

1. **AI-drafted first pass** — a frontier multilingual model
   produces the initial verse-by-verse draft with full per-verse
   provenance, following the same methodology used for English
   (DOCTRINE.md translation philosophy §§1–5, per-verse YAML
   schema, `doctrine_reference` citations where relevant).
2. **AI-reviewer revision** — a second, distinct model reads the
   draft and flags awkward phrasing, dropped nuance, or places
   where the target language's idiom has drifted from the
   source's force. Revisions are discrete commits.
3. **Native-speaker community review** — before a language is
   declared stable, speakers of that language who are also
   familiar with the biblical source languages (or who have
   access to published lexicons in that language) audit the
   text and raise issues publicly.
4. **Public issue window** — a minimum public-review period with
   open GitHub issues before any language moves from "preview"
   to "stable."

**Supported languages will be disclosed publicly based on model
performance and feasibility.** Not every language has an AI model
capable of scholarly-accurate translation yet, and not every
language has a sufficient community of native-speaking reviewers
accessible to the project. We will publish the current supported-
language list, and the ready-but-not-yet-stable list, as we reach
the capability threshold for each. Languages that do not yet meet
the bar are named as such, not silently omitted.

Every language published under this program carries the same
CC-BY 4.0 license, the same per-verse provenance, the same
auditability. There is no tier system across languages — every
supported language gets the full People's Open Bible.
